first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing onboarding or signup friction improves early activation and time-to-value. This directly addresses both observed declines while better aligning with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose acquisition gains came with materially worse 30-day retention. Verify the two onboarding records before final commitment.

final.rationale: Run a guarded onboarding-simplification experiment only for SMB accounts identified as simple workspaces, with retention and qualified revenue as guardrails. The verified evidence shows gains in completion, activation, time-to-value, and qualified revenue, but also reveals a 9% increase in 60-day churn for complex workspaces, which must be excluded. Promotional pricing is not preferred despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence indicates material retention harm. Results should not be generalized beyond SMB/simple-workspace accounts.
